messages:
cara: Quick write-up of the hypersample two-pass tests I ran this morning. Trying to capture perf vs quality tradeoffs for 4-bit quantized variants + a light two-pass prefetch stage. TL;DR: 1.8–2.3x median token throughput improvement, but edge-case drop on commonsense QA (EM down ~2.5 pts).

ben: Nice, can you paste the exact config you used? interested in batch sizes and when warmup happens.

cara: Sure — config below. Inputs were 1k eval prompts, temp=0.2, top_p=0.95 for final decode. Prefetch stage: generate 8 tokens with top_k=5 sampling, then full greedy/CEA on cached KV.

cara: ```
model: llama-2-70b-q4
mode: hypersample-two-pass
pass1: { tokens: 8, sampler: top_k(5), temp: 0.8 }
pass2: { strategy: greedy+prefix-cache, beam: 1 }
batching: { max_tokens_per_batch: 4096, tokens_per_request: variable }
cpu_prefetch_threads: 2
quant: q4_0
metrics: [latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, EM, rouge-L]
```

alice: Quick note — we disabled runtime KV-sharding for these runs to avoid cross-GPU fetch noise. Might explain slightly worse tail latency on some seeds.

diego: Results table? numbers? I only need median and p95 for latency and token/sec. Also seed/replicate count.

cara: Copied results excerpt: 
- runs: 3 seeds (s1,s2,s3) over 1k prompts each
- median tokens/sec: baseline(q4 greedy)=420 tps, hypersample=930 tps (2.21x)
- p95 latency per request (512-token targets): baseline=320ms, hypersample=210ms (0.66x)
- EM (CommonsenseQA subset): baseline=72.4, hypersample=69.8 (delta -2.6)
- rouge-L (summaries subset): baseline=38.2, hypersample=37.9 (delta -0.3)

emma: Hmm EM drop is notable. Did you control for pass1 randomness? top_k=5 at temp=0.8 could produce misleading prefixes that bias final greedy output.

cara: Agreed — I also tried deterministic pass1 (top_k=1) — that gave smaller speedup (1.6x) but EM delta reduced to -0.9. So randomness in pass1 is the culprit on QA.

ben: Can you run a hybrid: pass1 stochastic but with n-hypotheses (beam-like) and then rerank in pass2? e.g., generate 3 prefix candidates, evaluate logprob under full model, pick best, then continue greedily. Might keep speed gains while recovering EM.

cara: I prototyped that quickly: 3-prefix rerank gives 1.9x tps and EM delta -0.7. Implementation note: rerank cost is small because scoring uses cached KV but still does O(prefixes * prefix_len) ops.

diego: What about eval methodology — are we using exact-match normalization? tokenization consistent? We need to ensure EM deltas aren't tokenization artifacts.

cara: Used existing harness: normalizing with whitespace + lowercasing, same tokenizer as model. I'll push raw outputs to S3 and link.

cara: S3 link: s3://redwood-internal/hypersample/1791234567/results.tar.gz (contains raw outputs, scores, and run configs) :file_folder: 

emma: Another angle — quantify uncertainty: compare pass1 prefix logits to pass2 final logits, measure KL divergence; high divergence correlates with quality drop. I can add that metric.

alice: Also bump the prefix length sweep: 4/8/12 tokens. My intuition: shorter prefix => less bias, but lower speed. Could plot tps vs EM for each prefix len.

cara: Did that: 4 tokens => 1.5x tps, EM delta -1.2; 8 tokens => 2.2x, delta -2.6; 12 tokens => 2.6x, delta -4.4. So tradeoff clear. Will attach a small plot in the follow-up.

ben: For production, my recommended default: 3-prefix rerank + prefix_len=6 and deterministic pass2. That gets ~2x tps with <1pt EM delta in our tests.

diego: Add regression tests to CI harness: smoke on datasets (SQA, NQ, CQA) with thresholded EM drops; block auto-rollout if >1.5 pt drop vs baseline.

ci-bot: Deploy job queued: perf-hypersample-canary on dedicated-pool-3. Job id #5812.

cara: Thanks — I'll prepare a short RFC with: methods, numbers, recommended defaults, and a checklist for canary gating. Will include the rerank hybrid as the conservative default.

emma: Great. If we proceed, plan a limited beta on low-risk internal features first. :thumbsup:
